notes: ACCESS: Akamai fronts this site - plain requests, r.jina.ai and WebFetch all 403, exactly as the Furniture-pass ledger recorded. curl_cffi impersonate=chrome131 via probe.py returned HTTP 200 on every URL and every API call in this session; chrome124 also worked on robots.txt. probe.py's 2s per-host gap was honoured. ROBOTS: https://www.garnethill.com/robots.txt fetched FIRST, before any other request (4,253 bytes). It contains exactly ONE user-agent group, 'User-agent: *'. There is NO group naming anthropic-ai, ClaudeBot, Claude-Web, Claude-SearchBot or any Claude agent, no wildcard Disallow: /, no Crawl-delay and no Content-Signal line. Its Disallow list is checkout/account/wishlist/gift-registry servlet views, /catalogs, /hidden-categories, /feature-stories, various *.jsp instrumentation views, /*ProductSearch, /*CSBJSONServices, and crucially '/*filter=', '/*sort=' and '/*bvstate=' - so NO facet, sort or filter URL was ever requested; every URL I touched is a bare /bedding-home/... category path, the four SiteMap_CAT_*_v2.xml files, or /UnbxdAPI?categoryId=... which matches no Disallow pattern in the file (the disallowed JSON endpoints are the named *JSONView / *CSBJSONServices servlets, not UnbxdAPI). TREE: two independent sources, agreeing exactly. (1) The complete category sitemap - SiteMap_CAT_001..004_v2.xml, 33+33+33+32 = 131 URLs, index confirms 005+ does not exist. I keyword-swept all 131 URLs for bath|shower|toilet|vanity|basin|sink|mirror|soap|towel|faucet|tap|wc|sanitary|cabinet|storage|hardware|hook. The ONLY bathroom-namespace hits are /bedding-home/bath/ and its three children /bath/towels/, /bath/shower-curtains/, /bath/bath-rugs-mats/ (plus the editorial /inspiration-hub/shopping-guides/towel-guide/, a how-to article, excluded). The whole home tree is: bedding-home/{all-home, bath/{towels, shower-curtains, bath-rugs-mats}, bedding/{bedding-basics, blankets-throws, comforters, duvet-covers, quilts, shams, sheets}, collections/, decor/{decorative-accessories, furniture, lighting, pillow-covers, throws}, features/, rugs/{area-rugs, doormats}}; everything else on the site is clothing, shoes and accessories. (2) The storefront's OWN Unbxd multilevel category facet: the response for categoryId 10141 (Bath) carries breadcrumb level 1 'Bedding & Home' -> level 2 'Bath' and a level-3 bucket listing exactly three values - Towels, Shower Curtains, Bath Rugs & Mats - and each child's own response terminates at level 3 with no level-4 bucket, i.e. all three are genuine leaves with no descendants. The two sources agree, so the tree is complete and nothing is hidden behind the PWA shell (the homepage HTML carries zero nav hrefs; this is an IBM WebSphere Commerce PWA, htmlClasses 'view-UnbxdBodyView area-CategoryView'). QTY METHOD: the rendered listing header cannot be read - the PLP grid is client-rendered and the served HTML contains no product-count element of any kind (I grepped the full 35KB of /bedding-home/bath/ for numberOfProducts/productCount/itemCount/results-count and got zero hits; it carries only the JSON-LD BreadcrumbList and the PWA bootstrap). The qty therefore comes from the storefront's own grid XHR - the exact request the PLP renders from - GET /UnbxdAPI?categoryId=<id>&returnRespAsJSON=true&isAPI=true&requesttype=ajax with header CBI-AJAX:1, field numberOfProducts. This is the same method and the same endpoint the Furniture pass validated on this site. VERIFICATION: (a) EXHAUSTION - numberOfProducts is a true total, not a page size. The endpoint's internal query carries rows=36; Bath Rugs & Mats reports 44/45 and the default call returns only 36 products, so I proved the remainder two ways: appending &rows=100 returned the full 45 product objects with 45 unique uniqueIds, and appending &unbxdStart=36 returned exactly the trailing 8 (36+8=44 on the earlier call). Towels (11), Shower Curtains (24), Bath (24) and Decorative Accessories (8) all return a products array whose length and unique-id count equal numberOfProducts exactly, on four categories of four different sizes. (b) BREADCRUMB MATCH - every response's facets.multilevel.breadcrumb was checked against the node requested: Bedding & Home > Bath > Towels, > Shower Curtains, > Bath Rugs & Mats, and each response's currentCategoryURL field echoes the exact path I requested (/bedding-home/bath/towels/ etc.). categoryName and the page <title> also match (Towels/'Bath Towels', Shower Curtains, Bath Rugs & Mats, All Bath). (c) DISCRIMINATION - 8, 11, 24, 24, 45, 512: not a site-wide constant. (d) DRIFT NOTE - Bath Rugs & Mats returned 44 on the first call and 45 about a minute later on a second call (a Plush Memory-Foam colourway coming back into stock); both calls were internally consistent (numberOfProducts == enumerated length) and the later, larger figure 45 is the one reported. (e) SKU-EXPANSION CALIBRATION, important - this storefront configures sku expansion PER CATEGORY, and the API's internal query shows it: Bath and Towels run with filter=-sku_expansion:true (collapsed, one card per style) while Bath Rugs & Mats and Shower Curtains run with filter=-sku_expansion:false (expanded, one card per colourway). That is why Shower Curtains reports 24 cards for 6 styles and Bath Rugs & Mats 45 cards for 4 styles. Each figure above is the number that category's OWN configured query returns - i.e. what the PLP actually renders - and no figure was taken from a sibling category's facet bucket, which would be computed under the wrong expansion setting (the Bath page's level-3 bucket reads Towels 11 / Shower Curtains 7 / Bath Rugs & Mats 4 under the collapsed config, while the Bath Rugs & Mats page's reads Bath Rugs & Mats 44 / Shower Curtains 24 / Towels 14 under the expanded one - the buckets are NOT comparable across configs and were not used as counts). CONCLUSION - NO BATHROOM FOUND: Garnet Hill is an apparel-and-bedding catalogue. Its 'Bath' department is a bath-LINEN department: all three of its leaves are textiles and route to Textile under rules 15, 16 and 20, and the parent itself holds only those textiles plus a cosmetic bag and a cross-merchandised side table. Per the brief's instruction I specifically checked for a genuine non-textile remainder before concluding - bath hardware, bathroom storage and bathroom mirrors - and there is none: across all 131 category URLs and the full Unbxd taxonomy there is no towel rail/bar/ring/hook, robe hook, toilet roll holder, soap dispenser or dish, toothbrush holder, bathroom shelf, bathroom cabinet, vanity unit, bathroom storage, bathroom or vanity mirror, basin, sink, toilet, bidet, bath, shower, enclosure, screen or tap node anywhere on the site. The single mirror in the catalogue (Scalloped-Edge Mirror Collection) sits in Decor > Decorative Accessories and is a decorative wall mirror, documented in review rather than skipped. Rows is therefore empty and all five findings are in review. CROSS-FILE DEDUP: lib/dedup.already_extracted() was run on all 8 candidate URLs (bath, bath/towels, bath/shower-curtains, bath/bath-rugs-mats, decor/decorative-accessories, decor/furniture, rugs/doormats, all-home). Exactly ONE hit - /bedding-home/decor/furniture/ -> Furniture.xlsx, 'Furniture' for this same company - which is the site's only furniture node and was never a Bathroom candidate. The index holds exactly one garnethill.com URL in total, that one. The other 7 returned None. Nothing was removed from rows for dedup; rows was empty on classification grounds.
